reference_observations.description: Friendly Club founding in 1850 excludes earlier periods but does not itself exclude 1851–55. Preserve the questioned 1877 attribution and missing accompanying documents; do not turn the conjecture into an exact writing day.
Emma handwriting with Charles signature does not automatically make the prose Emma own voice; distinguish this from an explicitly signed Emma addition.

corrections.description: Missing Leighton cover does not mean all substantive text is unavailable: the full Correa da Serra enclosure survives, copied from an older publication. Keep original observation, later copying/transmission and Darwin replication evidence separate.
This is a printed subscription form with Charles handwriting/signature, not simply a fragmentary heading or wholly individual Charles prose.
Huxley arrived may mean returned correspondence or an enclosure; first-pass wording must not establish a physical visit.

The old primary period hold allows a later Shrewsbury visit through November 1848; do not call its nominal 1841 date settled. Its actual location sketch has prior primary visual evidence, contrary to the no-figure claim.
Context is a joint Charles/Emma request in Erasmus handwriting with a later Charles date, not unqualified Charles prose from one day.
Missing first page does not erase the substantial surviving 43-block memorandum and three tables covering 1857–68. The accepted reading includes actual MathML and incomplete sampling limits.
Routine family or administrative subject is not a rejection criterion. Dates, authorship, surviving text and established counterpart determine scope.

summary: Eighteen targets and seven contexts rechecked through matched prior primary readings. Broad or disjoint dates and unidentified recipients remain held. Two William letters are leads for 1857; later family, Tegetmeier and club records are not made early by open XML bounds. No new links. Two targets lack a complete correspondence body, while 4217F has a separately preserved historical enclosure.
